title: Settings
subtitle: Changes take effect immediately and are saved for next time.
resetHint: Restores every tab to the values StarLight is installed with
clearPathHint: Go back to the default behavior

folders.defaultHint: Go back to the folder inside the work folder
folders.projectsUsage: Suggested when you save a new project or open one.
folders.exportsUsage: Starting point of the save dialog in the Export step.
folders.sessionsUsage: Suggested when you save the result of a live session as a project.
folders.label: Folders for projects, exports and sessions
folders.hint: Each one can also be outside the work folder, for example exports in a shared folder. A folder chosen separately stays the same even if you change the work folder.

general.workFolderHint: StarLight keeps your projects, exported images and live sessions here, each in its own folder. Folders are only created when needed, for example the first time you save a project. Files you’ve already saved aren’t moved when the folder changes.
general.defaultFolderHint: Go back to the default folder
general.defaultFolderHintPath: Go back to the default folder, {path}
general.reopenHint: At startup, StarLight reopens the last project you saved or opened, if the file is still in the same place. Recovering work after an unexpected shutdown and a FITS or XISF file opened with a double-click take priority.
general.reopen: Reopen the last project at startup
general.recoveryHint: While you work, StarLight periodically sets aside a copy of your unsaved work without touching your projects. If the program closes unexpectedly, because of a crash or a power cut, it offers to pick up from there when you reopen it.

performance.threadsHint: Number of frames analyzed and aligned at the same time, each by a separate thread. The automatic value uses the logical processors minus two, up to a maximum of twelve. Beyond this number, on processors with different types of cores, work doesn’t get faster and may slow down. This computer reports {count} logical processors: these are the computing streams the processor runs together, often twice the number of physical cores.
performance.memoryHint: Frames you’ve already opened stay in memory, so reopening them is instant. When the space runs out, the least recently used frame is released. The automatic value leaves at least a quarter of the installed memory to the system{ram}. Memory in use now: {used} of {budget}.
performance.lowPriorityHint: Lowers the priority of StarLight’s computations (analysis, alignment, stacking). During a long stack the computer stays responsive for other things, such as browsing or the program that controls the telescope, at the cost of a few extra seconds. Takes effect immediately.

computer.label: Settings chosen for this computer
computer.notYet: Not calculated yet: StarLight chooses them on its own shortly after the first startup.
computer.byHandOne: One item has been changed by hand since this choice.
computer.byHandOther: {count} items have been changed by hand since this choice.
computer.alreadyOptimal: The settings are already the recommended ones.
computer.measureFailed: Measurement failed: restart StarLight and try again.
computer.explain: The button measures the processors, memory and graphics card, shows what would change and applies it only if you confirm: all the items in this tab then take the calculated values. You can always change them by hand below, and they stay as you set them until you press the button again.

graphics.noneNoContext: none, because the viewer can’t create its graphics context
graphics.noneSoftware: none, drawing is done by the processor
graphics.unnamed: the system doesn’t report its name
graphics.gpuHint: On computers with two graphics cards, usually laptops, this decides which one to use. High performance requests the dedicated one: the sliders in Correct and Filters stay smooth even on large images. Power saving leaves the choice to the system, which usually uses the integrated one: the battery lasts longer but the viewer is less smooth. With a single card nothing changes. Takes effect at the next startup. In use now: {gpu}.
graphics.accelerationHint: With acceleration, the graphics card draws the viewer and computes corrections while you move the sliders. Turn it off only if the image appears black, checkered or flickering, or if StarLight closes on its own: drawing then moves to the processor, which always works but is much slower. Takes effect at the next startup.
graphics.restartNotice: Takes effect at the next startup: the graphics card and acceleration are chosen when the program opens. If there’s unsaved work, you’ll be asked whether to save it before restarting.

space.label: Disk space
space.hint: What StarLight stores on its own, outside your projects and exports, and how much space it takes. Clearing never touches your files.
space.windowHint: Pages and graphics card programs already prepared, which make startup faster. It’s recreated automatically: after clearing it, the first startup is a little slower.
space.windowHintPending: Pages and graphics card programs already prepared, which make startup faster. It’s recreated automatically: after clearing it, the first startup is a little slower. The graphics card part is in use now and will be cleared at the next startup.
space.logHint: The notes StarLight writes while it works, useful for understanding a problem. It stays on your computer and isn’t sent to anyone.
space.recoveryHint: Unsaved work set aside so you can pick it up after an unexpected shutdown. It’s deleted automatically when the program closes normally, so it can’t be cleared from here.
space.updatesHint: The latest version downloaded by the update check, ready to install. It’s replaced by the next one.
space.gaiaHint: Sky areas already downloaded for plate solving and color calibration. They’re kept in memory, not on disk, and are lost when the program closes. If you clear them, the next request downloads them again from the internet.
space.thumbnailsHint: The small images next to the frames. They’re kept in memory, not on disk, up to 800; they’re recreated when needed and lost when the program closes.

telescope.hintBefore: The folder where the telescope saves its frames. The Telescope button at the top opens the selection of frames to import directly here, and the live session in the Import step suggests it for watching. It can be a folder on this computer or a network path, for example
telescope.hintAfter: . If the field is empty, the Telescope button stays off and the live session suggests the last folder used.
telescope.placeholder: None: the Telescope button stays off

network.internetOn: StarLight uses the internet only to ask the Gaia catalog for the stars in an area of sky, sending the coordinates of the image center, to check whether a new version of the program is available, and to download the catalogs you install. The catalog is used for photometric color calibration and plate solving when the local stars aren’t installed or aren’t enough. Your images always stay on your computer.
network.internetOff: StarLight doesn’t connect to the internet. Photometric color calibration, plate solving with the Gaia catalog, catalog downloads and update checks aren’t available and show a notice if requested. Plate solving still works with the local stars if the package is installed and enabled. The plugin gallery, catalogs already installed and all other features work normally.
network.magnitudeHint: Photometric calibration asks the Gaia catalog for stars down to this magnitude. A higher value includes fainter stars, so more stars are matched but the download takes longer. The default value is {value}.

updates.checkHint: At startup, StarLight asks the update server whether there’s a version newer than {version}, the one you’re using. If there is, a window shows what’s new and asks whether to update now or later. No data about your images is sent to the server.
updates.internetOff: The check doesn’t run because internet access is turned off in the Network and catalogs tab.
updates.channelHint: Stable versions are more complete and better tested: they’re recommended for everyday use, although, as with any program, defects can never be ruled out entirely. Development versions bring new features sooner; when there isn’t a newer one, you still receive the latest stable version.
updates.devWarning: Development versions are less tested: they may contain unknown bugs, incomplete features or behavior that changes from one version to the next. They’re meant for those who want to try new features early and report problems. Save your work often and, if something goes wrong, you can switch back to stable versions only at any time.
updates.menuHint: The same check can also be started from the Help menu, with Check for updates.
